caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); font-family: Lora, serif; font-size: 16px; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: small;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #444444;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia;\"\u003EThis E log book also reflects my patient-centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: large;\"\u003EA 36 year old male, shop keeper by occupation, resident of Kolkata, West Bengal, came to OPD with chief complaints of vomiting since 2 months and pain in the abdomen since 2 months.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 2 months ago and then he developed vomiting which was insidious in onset, gradually progressive. The content of vomiting was food particles, yellow to green in color (non bilious), non projectile vomiting, no relation to pain. He had 4-5 episodes per day, occurs two to three hours after taking a meal. It occurs with both liquids and solids. It is associated with nausea, giddiness, constipation, belching, regurgitation. Appetite was normal. Aggravated on taking food and no relieving factors. Patient also complained of pain abdomen which was insidious in onset, non progressive, no radiation of pain. It was squeezing type and diffuse. There are no aggravating and relieving factors.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003EHistory of lethargy and weight loss. History of jaundice which was diagnosed incidently 2 months ago and visited a hospital in West bengal but no relief despite medications.\u003Cbr\u003ENo history of dysphagia, odynophagia, heartburn, indigestion, flatulence, diarrhoea, abdominal distention, hematemesis, melaena, urinary symptoms, chest pain, cold, cough.\u003Cbr\u003EEndoscopy was done in April outside hospital in Behar and was diagnosed as esophageal candidiasis, Lax LES, Pangastritis, Duodenitis.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cfont face=\"georgia\"\u003EDAILY ROUTINE:\u003C\/font\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EPatient wakes up around 6 in the morning and freshens up. Has his breakfast and goes to work where he is a shopkeeper . Takes his lunch during work and comes back home around 9 and takes his dinner.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EPAST HISTORY:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EPatient had no similar complaints in the past.\u003Cbr\u003ENot a known case of Hypertension, Diabetes, CAD, Epilepsy, TB, Thyroid disorders.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EFAMILY HISTORY:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003ENo similar complaints seen in the family.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EDiet\u0026nbsp;is mixed, appetite is normal, sleep inadequate since 2 months due to pain, bladder movements are regular, bowel movements- constipation since 2 months. History of weight loss since 2 months. Patient takes khaini since teenage. Patient is a non smoker, does not consume alcohol, chew tobacco etc. No known allergies. Not any kind of medication.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EGENERAL EXAMINATION:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EPatient is conscious, coherent, cooperative, well oriented to time, place and person. Thin built and poorly nourished.\u003Cbr\u003EPatient has pallor. No signs of icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, lymphadenopathy and edema.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EVitals:\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;Temp: afebrile\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; PR: 70\/min\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;RR: 16cpm\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;BP: 90\/60mmHg\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;SpO2: 98%\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EPer abdomen:\u003Cbr\u003EOn Inspection,\u0026nbsp; shape of abdomen is flat, no flank fullness, Umblicus is centrally placed and inverted. No pigmentation seen, No sinuses, scars, dilated veins, visible pulsations and hernial orifices.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EOn Palpation, all inspectory findings are confirmed. Kidney not palpable.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EOn Percussion, no fluid thrill or shifting dullness.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; I'll be sharing a couple of my most fascinating experiences during my postings in general medicine.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr \/\u003EAll my experiences were only possible because of the guidance I received from our HOD sir and my mentors. They have encouraged me in their unique way, sharing examples and taught me to pursue my dreams so I would like to express my gratitude to them.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EMy first ever encounter with a patient was when I was posted in the general medicine department and all of us were supposed to take up a patient's history and diagnose by ourselves. So, I happened to go to the AMC ward to take a patient's history. All of a sudden, I see a woman bawling her eyes out and obviously I could not stand for. I really wanted to get all the help she wanted with the knowledge I had so I tried to calm her down and take down a proper history.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EThe art of history taking involves the ability to recognize the interrelationship between the details of the medical history and the patient's personal history. Even though she was not in the right state to answer any of my questions, she did her best because she thought I could help her and that made me feel overwhelmed.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EShe was a very strong woman as she has had an amputation a year back and hysterectomy a year ago too. The husband was very accurate with the details of the surgeries and helped me with the history taking a little.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EIt was my first time ever, to examine a patient. I took consent and started my examination. Her per abdomen examination had positive findings of tenderness in the epigastric region which made me think of pancreatitis or GERD instantly. This was the only positive finding I had and was almost clue less so I begin to ask her the symptoms I know of pancreatitis and GERD.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EShe then tells me that the pain radiates to her back and reduces sometimes while laying down. There was no relation to any intake of food, vomiting and other gastric symptoms so it led me to believe that it was pancreatitis. I asked my mentor and the provisional diagnosis turned out to be pancreatitis. It made me satisfied that I was close to her diagnosis but little did i know that she had been misdiagnosed by me until and after I saw her endoscopy findings. I learnt a lot after that. History taking is as important as the laboratory findings.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EThis made me question my ability of a proper history taking, per abdomen examination, where I lacked. From this onwards, I have been constantly motivated to better than the previous day and it made me impelling.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EHere is the blog link of this case:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/rohithjampanirollno185.blogspot.com\/2023\/03\/60-year-old-female-with-pain-vomiting.html\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: medium;\"\u003EThe true method of knowledge is experiment. The more I learn, The self confidence I will have.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #202124;\"\u003EIn closing, I want to remind you to never stop learning, and never forget that\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #202124;\"\u003E medicine is an art practiced by doctors. We bring to people not only technology and training, but also our humanity and caring.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr \/\u003EThank you!\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"replies","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/rohithjampanirollno185.blogspot.com\/feeds\/7978343478660981244\/comments\/default","title":"Post Comments"},{"rel":"replies","type":"text/html","href":"https:\/\/rohithjampanirollno185.blogspot.com\/2023\/06\/my-experiences-with-general-cellular.html#comment-form","title":"0 Comments"},{"rel":"edit","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/4087256910463629476\/posts\/default\/7978343478660981244"},{"rel":"self","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/4087256910463629476\/posts\/default\/7978343478660981244"},{"rel":"alternate","type":"text/html","href":"https:\/\/rohithjampanirollno185.blogspot.com\/2023\/06\/my-experiences-with-general-cellular.html","title":"MY EXPERIENCES WITH GENERAL CELLULAR AND NEURAL CELLULAR PATHOLOGY IN A CASE BASED BLENDED LEARNING ECOSYSTEM'S CBBLE"}],"author":[{"name":{"$t":"Rohith Jampani"},"uri":{"$t":"http:\/\/www.blogger.com\/profile\/17937172422277244137"},"email":{"$t":"noreply@blogger.com"},"gd$image":{"rel":"http://schemas.google.com/g/2005#thumbnail","width":"16","height":"16","src":"https:\/\/img1.blogblog.com\/img\/b16-rounded.gif"}}],"thr$total":{"$t":"0"}},{"id":{"$t":"tag:blogger.com,1999:blog-4087256910463629476.post-3612362803763403009"},"published":{"$t":"2023-03-29T07:23:00.001-07:00"},"updated":{"$t":"2023-05-31T01:32:21.865-07:00"},"title":{"type":"text","$t":"60 year old female with pain, vomiting and burning micturition"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;
